Serious psychotic effects (deper- sonalisation and anxiety) developed in a healthy subject who took a standard 3-day course of oral chloroquine for the treat- ment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria, as part of a clinical study. Three weeks after completing the course she still had seri- ous concentration problems and her symptoms gradually re- solved over the next 4 months.1 1. Telgt DS, et al. Serious psychiatric symptoms after chloroquine treatment following experimental malaria infection. Ann Phar- macother 2005; 39: 551–4. Effects on the muscles. The myopathy induced by chloro- quine is characterised by progressive weakness and atrophy of proximal muscles and can develop insidiously after periods of therapy ranging from a few weeks to a few years.1 There are of- ten mild sensory changes, depression of tendon reflexes, and ab- normal nerve conduction studies suggestive of an associated pe- ripheral neuropathy.
